title: Choose your neighbors (Avot 1:7)
hookLine: Nittai: keep far from a bad neighbor, and don't give up on justice
carry: kindness isn't the same as closeness
last: JUDGE ON THE SIDE OF MERIT.

cards: Spend a week with a friend who complains about everything, and the complaining can rub off. Sit near the coworker who cuts corners, and your corners start getting shorter.

Scroll a certain feed for an hour, and you come away a little meaner than you went in. People catch moods and habits from those around them, the way they catch colds. Joshua ben Perachyah said judge everyone favorably.
His teaching partner, Nittai of Arbel, answers with a warning: being generous about people doesn't mean living next door to everything.

teach.h: KEEP FAR FROM A BAD NEIGHBOR.
teach.b: Nittai of Arbel says three things, in paraphrase. Keep far from a bad neighbor. Don't attach yourself to a wicked person.

And don't give up on justice; or, more literally, don't despair of retribution. Start with the neighbor. The advice is practical: when you choose where to live, who to work beside, who to be close to, choose with care.
Rashi, reading a detail in the book of Numbers, notices who camped next to whom in the desert. The tribe camped beside a well-known rebel was drawn into his rebellion.
The tribes camped beside Moses grew great in learning.

teach.h: WOE TO THE WICKED AND HIS NEIGHBOR.
teach.b: And Rashi passes on a saying: woe to the wicked, and woe to his neighbor; good for the righteous, and good for his neighbor. These two sayings sit side by side in Avot, from a pair of teachers. Judge everyone favorably.
Keep far from a bad neighbor. Avot keeps both. You can give someone the benefit of the doubt and still choose not to sit next to them every day.
Kindness isn't the same as closeness. Then the third line: don't despair of retribution. Commentators hear it two ways.
Don't envy people who seem to get away with harm; justice isn't finished yet.
And don't get complacent yourself when things go well; nobody's beyond consequences. Either way, Nittai is saying the world has a moral shape, even when it's hard to see.

how: Jewish teaching gives weight to choosing one's community and surroundings, and Nittai's advice is cited when people choose a neighborhood, a school or friends.

o: the sage who said keep far from a bad neighbor
the scribe who first wrote down the Mishnah
a prophet who warned Israel against idols

games.q: Nittai's three sayings — tap the pairs.
p: woe to the wicked and his neighbor

s: judging favorably means staying close to everyone
Avot pairs judge everyone favorably with keep far from a bad neighbor: kindness isn't closeness.
Nittai and Joshua ben Perachyah were a teaching pair
Avot lists them together as the second of the pairs.
don't despair of retribution has only one accepted meaning
commentators read it as don't envy those who seem to escape, and as don't grow complacent yourself.

games.q: a coworker who constantly cuts corners wants to share your desk. you've already decided to judge him kindly. what does Nittai add?
o: kindness means you should sit together.
you can think well of him and still keep some distance.
games.why: Nittai says keep far from a bad neighbor. alongside his partner's judge everyone favorably, it means: generous in judgment, careful in closeness.

practice: Think about what you're close to every day, people, places, feeds, habits, group chats, and whether one reliably leaves you worse: not a person to condemn, just a neighbor to move away from.
Picture putting a little distance there, muting it, sitting elsewhere, spending the time somewhere better. Then think of one good neighbor to move toward.

wordCard.voice: Nittai, the sage who taught keep far from a bad neighbor, and don't give up on justice, paired beside his partner's call to judge everyone favorably.

orig.note: Hebrew: keep far from a bad neighbor. Nittai of Arbel's first saying (Avot 1:7).

carryVoice: Your line: kindness isn't the same as closeness. Generous about people, careful about neighbors. Two hundred forty days, and counting.
